nsp-full-weekly.label: Full new State Pension
nsp-full-weekly.definition: The full weekly rate of the new State Pension, before any protected payment or extra pension from deferral.
nsp-full-weekly.population: People who reached State Pension age on or after 6 April 2016 and have the National Insurance record needed for the full rate.
nsp-full-weekly.geography: Great Britain. Northern Ireland sets the same rate through its own order, which we did not read.
nsp-full-weekly.table_reference: Part: What you'll get. Confirmed in the rates publication (row: New State Pension, full rate) and in article 6(1) of the Up-rating Order 2026.
nsp-full-weekly.passage: The full rate of new State Pension is £241.30 a week.
nsp-full-weekly.qualifications: A full rate, not everyone's payment. The amount a person gets depends on their National Insurance record. Some people get less. Some get more, because of a protected payment, Additional State Pension or deferral.
nsp-full-weekly.next_review: When the rates for 2027/28 are confirmed, and again when the up-rating takes effect in April 2027. Check the date in the up-rating order.

nsp-full-52-weeks.label: Full new State Pension over 52 weeks
nsp-full-52-weeks.definition: 52 weekly amounts at the full new State Pension rate.
nsp-full-52-weeks.table_reference: Calculated by this site from the weekly rate.
nsp-full-52-weeks.qualifications: An equivalent, not what a person receives in a tax year. Rates change in April, payments are made every 4 weeks, and HM Revenue and Customs counts one week at the old rate and 51 weeks at the new rate for tax.
nsp-full-52-weeks.next_review: When the rates for 2027/28 are confirmed, and again when the up-rating takes effect in April 2027. Check the date in the up-rating order.

bsp-full-weekly.label: Full basic State Pension
bsp-full-weekly.definition: The full weekly rate of the basic State Pension (Category A or B), before any Additional State Pension, Graduated Retirement Benefit or extra pension from deferral.
bsp-full-weekly.population: People who reached State Pension age before 6 April 2016 and have the National Insurance record needed for the full rate.
bsp-full-weekly.geography: Great Britain. Northern Ireland sets the same rate through its own order, which we did not read.
bsp-full-weekly.table_reference: Part: How much you get. Confirmed in the rates publication (row: Category A or B basic pension) and in article 4(2) of the Up-rating Order 2026.
bsp-full-weekly.passage: The full basic State Pension is £184.90 per week.
bsp-full-weekly.qualifications: A full rate, not everyone's payment. The amount a person gets depends on their National Insurance record. Some people get less. Some get more, because of a protected payment, Additional State Pension or deferral. Many people on the basic State Pension also get Additional State Pension, so the basic rate alone understates what they receive.
bsp-full-weekly.next_review: When the rates for 2027/28 are confirmed, and again when the up-rating takes effect in April 2027. Check the date in the up-rating order.

cpi-linked-uprating-2026.label: Increase applied to protected payments, Additional State Pension and deferral increases
cpi-linked-uprating-2026.definition: The percentage increase applied in April 2026 to the parts of the State Pension that do not follow the triple lock.
cpi-linked-uprating-2026.table_reference: Rows: Protected Payment; Additional pension; Increments. 2026/27 column. Also articles 4(3) and 6(3)(b) of the Up-rating Order 2026.
cpi-linked-uprating-2026.qualifications: GOV.UK says the protected payment and deferral increases rise in line with the Consumer Prices Index. The Order gives the percentage for Additional State Pension but does not name the index.
cpi-linked-uprating-2026.next_review: When the rates for 2027/28 are confirmed, and again when the up-rating takes effect in April 2027. Check the date in the up-rating order.

nsp-min-qualifying-years.label: Qualifying years needed for any new State Pension
nsp-min-qualifying-years.definition: The usual minimum number of qualifying years on a National Insurance record to get any new State Pension.
nsp-min-qualifying-years.population: People who reach State Pension age on or after 6 April 2016.
nsp-min-qualifying-years.geography: United Kingdom rule as described on GOV.UK.
nsp-min-qualifying-years.passage: You'll need 10 qualifying years on your National Insurance record to get any new State Pension.
nsp-min-qualifying-years.qualifications: GOV.UK describes exceptions, for example for some people who lived or worked abroad.
nsp-min-qualifying-years.next_review: Each April, and sooner if the rule is changed in law.

nsp-full-rate-years.label: Qualifying years for the full rate, for a record that began after April 2016
nsp-full-rate-years.definition: The number of qualifying years needed for the full new State Pension where the National Insurance record started after April 2016.
nsp-full-rate-years.population: People whose National Insurance record started after April 2016.
nsp-full-rate-years.geography: United Kingdom rule as described on GOV.UK.
nsp-full-rate-years.passage: If your National Insurance record started after April 2016 you will need 35 qualifying years to get the full rate of new State Pension.
nsp-full-rate-years.qualifications: 35 years does not guarantee the full rate for everyone. A record that began before April 2016 is converted into a starting amount, which is reduced for periods of contracting out. GOV.UK says people who were contracted out will usually need more than 35 years.
nsp-full-rate-years.next_review: Each April, and sooner if the rule is changed in law.

nsp-per-qualifying-year.label: New State Pension added by each qualifying year after 5 April 2016
nsp-per-qualifying-year.definition: The approximate weekly amount each extra qualifying year adds, up to the full rate.
nsp-per-qualifying-year.population: People with a starting amount below the full rate.
nsp-per-qualifying-year.geography: United Kingdom rule as described on GOV.UK.
nsp-per-qualifying-year.qualifications: GOV.UK gives the figure as 'about £6.89'. It matches the 2026/27 full rate divided by 35.
nsp-per-qualifying-year.next_review: When the rates for 2027/28 are confirmed, and again when the up-rating takes effect in April 2027. Check the date in the up-rating order.

pension-credit-single.label: Pension Credit standard minimum guarantee, single person
pension-credit-single.definition: The weekly income level that Guarantee Credit tops a single person up to.
pension-credit-single.population: People over State Pension age on a low income who claim.
pension-credit-single.geography: Great Britain. Northern Ireland has its own scheme.
pension-credit-single.table_reference: Pension Credit rows: Standard minimum guarantee, single. 2026/27 column.
pension-credit-single.qualifications: Not automatic. It must be claimed. Extra amounts apply for severe disability, caring and some housing costs.
pension-credit-single.next_review: When the rates for 2027/28 are confirmed, and again when the up-rating takes effect in April 2027. Check the date in the up-rating order.

pension-credit-couple.label: Pension Credit standard minimum guarantee, couple
pension-credit-couple.definition: The joint weekly income level that Guarantee Credit tops a couple up to.
pension-credit-couple.population: Couples over State Pension age on a low income who claim.
pension-credit-couple.geography: Great Britain. Northern Ireland has its own scheme.
pension-credit-couple.table_reference: Pension Credit rows: Standard minimum guarantee, couple. 2026/27 column.
pension-credit-couple.qualifications: Not automatic. It must be claimed.
pension-credit-couple.next_review: When the rates for 2027/28 are confirmed, and again when the up-rating takes effect in April 2027. Check the date in the up-rating order.

pension-credit-take-up.label: Pension Credit take-up
pension-credit-take-up.definition: The estimated share of families entitled to Pension Credit who claimed it.
pension-credit-take-up.population: Entitled pensioner families in private households.
pension-credit-take-up.table_reference: Main findings, and Table PC1 of the Pension Credit tables.
pension-credit-take-up.passage: 62% of those entitled to Pension Credit claimed the benefit in FYE 2024, which was a decrease from FYE 2023, when 65% claimed the benefit – this difference is not statistically significant
pension-credit-take-up.qualifications: A survey-based estimate. The fall from the year before is not statistically significant. The method changed in this year.
pension-credit-take-up.next_review: 22 October 2026, when the estimates for the financial year ending 2025 are due.

pension-credit-unclaimed.label: Pension Credit that went unclaimed
pension-credit-unclaimed.definition: The estimated total Pension Credit that entitled families did not claim.
pension-credit-unclaimed.population: Entitled pensioner families in private households who did not claim.
pension-credit-unclaimed.table_reference: Table PC2 of the Pension Credit tables.
pension-credit-unclaimed.qualifications: A survey-based estimate. Rounded to the nearest £10 million in the source.

pension-credit-non-recipients.label: Entitled families not receiving Pension Credit
pension-credit-non-recipients.definition: The estimated number of families entitled to Pension Credit who did not receive it.
pension-credit-non-recipients.population: Entitled pensioner families in private households.
pension-credit-non-recipients.table_reference: File pension_credit_tables_fye_2324.ods. Sheet PC1, table PC1, block "Estimated number of entitled non-recipients (with range)", row FYE 2024, column "Pension Credit Overall": cell B36, 820, in thousands, rounded to the nearest 10,000. Range 740 to 910 thousand.
pension-credit-non-recipients.qualifications: A survey-based estimate. Rounded to the nearest 10,000 in the source.

personal-allowance.label: Standard Personal Allowance for Income Tax
personal-allowance.definition: The amount of income a person can have in a tax year before Income Tax is due.
personal-allowance.table_reference: Section: Income Tax rates and bands.
personal-allowance.qualifications: The allowance was already fixed at £12,570 up to the tax year 2027 to 2028. Section 10 of the Finance Act 2026 extends that to 2028 to 2029, 2029 to 2030 and 2030 to 2031. The allowance is reduced for income over £100,000.
personal-allowance.next_review: When rates and limits for 2027 to 2028 are published.

deferral-weeks-new.label: Weeks of deferral for each 1% increase, new State Pension
deferral-weeks-new.definition: The number of weeks a person defers the new State Pension for each 1% added to the weekly payment.
deferral-weeks-new.population: People who reached State Pension age on or after 6 April 2016.
deferral-weeks-new.table_reference: Part: If you reach State Pension age on or after 6 April 2016.
deferral-weeks-new.passage: For every 9 weeks you defer, you'll get 1% added to your regular weekly pension payment for life.
deferral-weeks-new.qualifications: GOV.UK says it takes over 15 years to get back 52 weeks of deferred full new State Pension. Extra pension cannot build up while the person gets certain benefits.
deferral-weeks-new.next_review: Each April, and sooner if the rule is changed in law.

deferral-weeks-basic.label: Weeks of deferral for each 1% increase, basic State Pension
deferral-weeks-basic.definition: The number of weeks a person defers the basic State Pension for each 1% added to the weekly payment.
deferral-weeks-basic.population: People who reached State Pension age before 6 April 2016.
deferral-weeks-basic.table_reference: Part: If you reached State Pension age before 6 April 2016.
deferral-weeks-basic.passage: For every 5 weeks you defer, you'll get 1% of that amount added to your regular payment for life.
deferral-weeks-basic.next_review: Each April, and sooner if the rule is changed in law.

attendance-allowance-lower.label: Attendance Allowance, lower rate
attendance-allowance-lower.definition: The lower weekly rate of Attendance Allowance.
attendance-allowance-lower.population: People over State Pension age who need help or supervision because of a disability or health condition.
attendance-allowance-lower.geography: England and Wales. Scotland has Pension Age Disability Payment.
attendance-allowance-lower.qualifications: Not means-tested. It must be claimed.
attendance-allowance-lower.next_review: When the rates for 2027/28 are confirmed, and again when the up-rating takes effect in April 2027. Check the date in the up-rating order.

attendance-allowance-higher.label: Attendance Allowance, higher rate
attendance-allowance-higher.definition: The higher weekly rate of Attendance Allowance.
attendance-allowance-higher.population: People over State Pension age who need help or supervision day and night, or who are nearing the end of life.
attendance-allowance-higher.geography: England and Wales. Scotland has Pension Age Disability Payment.
attendance-allowance-higher.qualifications: Not means-tested. It must be claimed.
attendance-allowance-higher.next_review: When the rates for 2027/28 are confirmed, and again when the up-rating takes effect in April 2027. Check the date in the up-rating order.

winter-fuel-income-limit.label: Income above which a Winter Fuel Payment is recovered
winter-fuel-income-limit.definition: The individual total income above which HM Revenue and Customs takes the Winter Fuel Payment back through the tax system.
winter-fuel-income-limit.population: People who receive a Winter Fuel Payment.
winter-fuel-income-limit.geography: England, Wales and Northern Ireland. Scotland has Pension Age Winter Heating Payment.
winter-fuel-income-limit.table_reference: Guide overview. Also Schedule 10 to the Finance Act 2026.
winter-fuel-income-limit.passage: If your total income is over £35,000, HMRC will take your Winter Fuel Payment back. Your partner's income does not count towards your total.
winter-fuel-income-limit.qualifications: The payment is between £100 and £300. People who get Pension Credit are not charged.
winter-fuel-income-limit.next_review: Before winter 2027 to 2028, when the government confirms the income limit for that winter.

sp-recipients.label: People receiving the State Pension
sp-recipients.definition: People receiving any State Pension at a point in time.
sp-recipients.geography: The release covers DWP benefits in Great Britain.
sp-recipients.passage: There were 13 million people receiving the State Pension at March 2026, an increase of 260,000 compared to February 2025.
sp-recipients.qualifications: A count at one date. The comparison with February 2025 covers 13 months. The release does not say whether recipients living abroad are included. For comparison, the department's expenditure tables give a total of about the same size, and that total includes people paid outside the UK.

nsp-recipients.label: People receiving the new State Pension
nsp-recipients.definition: People receiving the new State Pension at a point in time.
nsp-recipients.geography: The release covers DWP benefits in Great Britain.
nsp-recipients.passage: At March 2026 there were 5.4 million people receiving nSP

nsp-mean-weekly.label: Mean new State Pension paid
nsp-mean-weekly.definition: The mean weekly amount of State Pension in payment, including any protected payment or Additional State Pension.
nsp-mean-weekly.geography: The release covers DWP benefits in Great Britain.
nsp-mean-weekly.qualifications: Amounts at March 2026 rates, before the April 2026 increase. They must not be compared with the 2026/27 full rate without saying so. The release does not say whether recipients living abroad are included.

nsp-mean-weekly-men.label: Mean new State Pension paid to men

nsp-mean-weekly-men.geography: The release covers DWP benefits in Great Britain.

nsp-mean-weekly-women.label: Mean new State Pension paid to women
nsp-mean-weekly-women.definition: The mean weekly amount of State Pension in payment, including any protected payment or Additional State Pension.
nsp-mean-weekly-women.population: Women receiving the new State Pension.
nsp-mean-weekly-women.geography: The release covers DWP benefits in Great Britain.
nsp-mean-weekly-women.qualifications: Amounts at March 2026 rates, before the April 2026 increase. They must not be compared with the 2026/27 full rate without saying so. The release does not say whether recipients living abroad are included.

pre2016-mean-weekly.label: Mean pre-2016 State Pension paid
pre2016-mean-weekly.definition: The mean weekly amount of State Pension in payment, including any protected payment or Additional State Pension.
pre2016-mean-weekly.population: People receiving the pre-2016 State Pension.
pre2016-mean-weekly.geography: The release covers DWP benefits in Great Britain.
pre2016-mean-weekly.qualifications: Amounts at March 2026 rates, before the April 2026 increase. They must not be compared with the 2026/27 full rate without saying so. The release does not say whether recipients living abroad are included.

pre2016-mean-weekly-men.label: Mean pre-2016 State Pension paid to men
pre2016-mean-weekly-men.definition: The mean weekly amount of State Pension in payment, including any protected payment or Additional State Pension.
pre2016-mean-weekly-men.population: Men receiving the pre-2016 State Pension.
pre2016-mean-weekly-men.geography: The release covers DWP benefits in Great Britain.
pre2016-mean-weekly-men.qualifications: Amounts at March 2026 rates, before the April 2026 increase. They must not be compared with the 2026/27 full rate without saying so. The release does not say whether recipients living abroad are included.

pre2016-mean-weekly-women.label: Mean pre-2016 State Pension paid to women
pre2016-mean-weekly-women.definition: The mean weekly amount of State Pension in payment, including any protected payment or Additional State Pension.
pre2016-mean-weekly-women.population: Women receiving the pre-2016 State Pension.
pre2016-mean-weekly-women.geography: The release covers DWP benefits in Great Britain.
pre2016-mean-weekly-women.qualifications: Amounts at March 2026 rates, before the April 2026 increase. They must not be compared with the 2026/27 full rate without saying so. The release does not say whether recipients living abroad are included.

sp-mean-weekly.label: Mean State Pension paid, both systems
sp-mean-weekly.definition: The mean weekly amount of State Pension in payment, including any protected payment or Additional State Pension.
sp-mean-weekly.geography: The release covers DWP benefits in Great Britain.
sp-mean-weekly.qualifications: Amounts at March 2026 rates, before the April 2026 increase. They must not be compared with the 2026/27 full rate without saying so. The release does not say whether recipients living abroad are included.

sp-paid-overseas.label: State Pension recipients living outside the UK
sp-paid-overseas.definition: The average number of State Pension recipients living outside the United Kingdom over the financial year.
sp-paid-overseas.table_reference: File outturn-and-forecast-tables-spring-forecast-2026.xlsx. Sheet "State Pension", block "State Pension caseload, thousands", row "State Pension paid outside UK included above", column 2024/25 Outturn: cell CB38, 1,102 thousand.
sp-paid-overseas.qualifications: An average over the year, rounded to the nearest 1,000. It does not show how many live in countries where the pension is not increased each year.
sp-paid-overseas.next_review: Each April, and sooner if the Department for Work and Pensions publishes its next benefit expenditure and caseload tables.

sp-spend-2024-25.label: State Pension spending, latest outturn
sp-spend-2024-25.definition: Total spending on the State Pension in the financial year, in cash terms.
sp-spend-2024-25.population: All State Pension recipients covered by DWP.
sp-spend-2024-25.geography: Great Britain, and people living overseas who receive the UK State Pension. Northern Ireland is not included.
sp-spend-2024-25.gross_net: Gross spending, before any tax paid by recipients
sp-spend-2024-25.table_reference: File outturn-and-forecast-tables-spring-forecast-2026.xlsx. Sheet "State Pension", block "£ million, nominal terms", row Total, column 2024/25 Outturn: cell CB4, £136,584.4 million. The same value is in Table 1a, cell CB63.
sp-spend-2024-25.qualifications: This is not all spending on older people. It covers all State Pension components: basic, new, Additional State Pension, Graduated Retirement Benefit, protected payments, lump sums and the non-contributory pension. Other official figures for the same year differ because they use a different accounting basis or coverage.
sp-spend-2024-25.next_review: When the Office for Budget Responsibility publishes its next forecast and DWP updates its tables.

sp-spend-2026-27.label: State Pension spending, current year forecast
sp-spend-2026-27.definition: Forecast total spending on the State Pension in the financial year, in cash terms.
sp-spend-2026-27.population: All State Pension recipients covered by DWP.
sp-spend-2026-27.geography: Great Britain, and people living overseas who receive the UK State Pension. Northern Ireland is not included.
sp-spend-2026-27.gross_net: Gross spending, before any tax paid by recipients
sp-spend-2026-27.table_reference: File outturn-and-forecast-tables-spring-forecast-2026.xlsx. Sheet "State Pension", block "£ million, nominal terms", row Total, column 2026/27 Forecast: cell CD4, £154,174.5 million. The same value is in Table 1a, cell CD63.
sp-spend-2026-27.qualifications: This is not all spending on older people. It covers all State Pension components: basic, new, Additional State Pension, Graduated Retirement Benefit, protected payments, lump sums and the non-contributory pension. Other official figures for the same year differ because they use a different accounting basis or coverage. A forecast made in spring 2026.
sp-spend-2026-27.next_review: When the Office for Budget Responsibility publishes its next forecast and DWP updates its tables.

pensioner-benefits-2024-25.label: All DWP benefit spending directed at pensioners
pensioner-benefits-2024-25.definition: DWP spending on all benefits paid to pensioners, including the State Pension, Pension Credit, housing benefits and disability benefits.
pensioner-benefits-2024-25.geography: Great Britain, with some benefits covering England and Wales only.
pensioner-benefits-2024-25.table_reference: File outturn-and-forecast-tables-spring-forecast-2026.xlsx. Sheet "Table 2a" (expenditure by age group, £ million, nominal terms), row "Total Expenditure directed at pensioners", column 2024/25 Outturn: cell CB129, £164,942.6 million.
pensioner-benefits-2024-25.qualifications: Wider than the State Pension. It still leaves out health and social care spending.
pensioner-benefits-2024-25.next_review: When the Office for Budget Responsibility publishes its next forecast and DWP updates its tables.

sp-share-gdp-2025-26.label: State Pension spending as a share of the economy
sp-share-gdp-2025-26.definition: State Pension spending as a share of gross domestic product.
sp-share-gdp-2025-26.table_reference: Table 3.1: Baseline primary spending scenario, row: State pension.
sp-share-gdp-2025-26.qualifications: An estimate consistent with the March 2026 forecast.
sp-share-gdp-2025-26.next_review: July 2027, when the next report is expected.

sp-share-gdp-2075-76.label: Projected State Pension spending as a share of the economy
sp-share-gdp-2075-76.definition: Projected State Pension spending as a share of gross domestic product, if current policy continued.
sp-share-gdp-2075-76.table_reference: Table 3.1: Baseline primary spending scenario, row: State pension.
sp-share-gdp-2075-76.passage: In the baseline scenario, state pension spending is projected to increase from 5 per cent to 9 per cent of GDP in the 50 years to 2075-76.
sp-share-gdp-2075-76.qualifications: A 50-year projection, not a forecast. It assumes the triple lock continues and adds 0.56 percentage points a year to earnings growth, that State Pension age reaches 68 between 2037 and 2039 and 69 between 2073 and 2075, and the 2024-based population projections. The July 2025 report gave 7.7% for 2073-74 on different assumptions, so the two editions cannot be compared directly.

tl-share-of-rise.label: Part of the projected rise attributed to the triple lock
tl-share-of-rise.definition: The part of the projected long-term rise in State Pension spending that the Office for Budget Responsibility attributes to the triple lock.
tl-share-of-rise.passage: In the baseline scenario, the triple lock drives 1.2 per cent of GDP out of the overall 3.6 per cent of GDP long-term increase in state pension spending.
tl-share-of-rise.qualifications: The rest of the rise comes mainly from an older population. The same report also says that earnings uprating would lower spending by 1.8% of GDP by the end of the period. The report does not explain the difference between the two figures, so we quote each with its own wording.

tl-premium-obr.label: Assumed yearly gap between the triple lock and earnings growth
tl-premium-obr.definition: The amount by which the Office for Budget Responsibility assumes triple lock increases exceed earnings growth each year on average.
tl-premium-obr.passage: Our latest estimate of this wedge is 0.56 percentage points
tl-premium-obr.qualifications: Based on inflation and earnings since 1990. The 2025 report showed that the result is sensitive to the period chosen: 0.11 points on a calmer period and 0.93 points on a more volatile one.
tl-premium-obr.next_review: July 2027, with the next Fiscal risks and sustainability report.

tl-cost-vs-earnings-2029-30.label: Extra yearly spending from the triple lock compared with earnings uprating
tl-cost-vs-earnings-2029-30.definition: The estimated extra State Pension spending in one year because the triple lock, not earnings uprating, has been used since 2012.
tl-cost-vs-earnings-2029-30.gross_net: Gross. No allowance for tax or benefit offsets.
tl-cost-vs-earnings-2029-30.passage: we estimate that uprating by the triple lock rather than earnings will have added £15.5 billion (0.5 per cent of GDP) to state pension spending annually by 2029-30
tl-cost-vs-earnings-2029-30.qualifications: A difference from a counterfactual, not a bill. Part outturn and part forecast. It is the built-up effect of past increases on one year's spending. It is not money that would be saved by changing the rule now.
tl-cost-vs-earnings-2029-30.next_review: July 2027, with the next Fiscal risks and sustainability report. A July 2026 edition exists; check whether it updates this figure.

tl-cost-vs-cpi-2029-30.label: Extra yearly spending from the triple lock compared with prices uprating
tl-cost-vs-cpi-2029-30.definition: The estimated extra State Pension spending in one year because the triple lock, not uprating by the Consumer Prices Index, has been used since 2012.
tl-cost-vs-cpi-2029-30.gross_net: Gross. No allowance for tax or benefit offsets.
tl-cost-vs-cpi-2029-30.passage: Relative to CPI uprating, we expect that the triple lock will have added £22.9 billion to annual state pension spending by 2029-30.
tl-cost-vs-cpi-2029-30.qualifications: A difference from a counterfactual, not a bill. Part outturn and part forecast.
tl-cost-vs-cpi-2029-30.next_review: July 2027, with the next Fiscal risks and sustainability report. A July 2026 edition exists; check whether it updates this figure.

tl-cost-initial-assumption.label: What the triple lock was first assumed to cost by 2029-30
tl-cost-initial-assumption.definition: The extra yearly spending, compared with earnings uprating, that the triple lock would have produced by 2029-30 on the assumption made in 2010.
tl-cost-initial-assumption.passage: This is around three times higher than the £5.2 billion we estimate the triple lock would have cost by that point under initial assumptions
tl-cost-initial-assumption.qualifications: A reconstruction made in 2025, not a figure published in 2010. 'Three times' compares two differences from earnings uprating. It does not mean State Pension spending is three times what was expected.
tl-cost-initial-assumption.next_review: July 2027, with the next Fiscal risks and sustainability report. A July 2026 edition exists; check whether it updates this figure.

tl-cost-ifs-2023.label: Extra yearly spending from the triple lock, 2023 estimate
tl-cost-ifs-2023.definition: The estimated extra State Pension spending in a year because of the triple lock, compared with uprating by prices or by earnings since 2011.
tl-cost-ifs-2023.passage: the government now spends an additional £11 billion per year on state pensions as a result of the triple lock
tl-cost-ifs-2023.qualifications: A difference from a counterfactual. The authors say prices and earnings uprating gave very similar results over that period.
tl-cost-ifs-2023.next_review: Each April. It comes from a single study, so it changes only if the Institute for Fiscal Studies publishes newer work that replaces it.

tl-cost-rf-gross-2026.label: Extra yearly spending from the triple lock, 2026 estimate, gross
tl-cost-rf-gross-2026.definition: The estimated extra State Pension spending this year compared with earnings-linked uprating since 2012.
tl-cost-rf-gross-2026.passage: The OBR estimates spending... would have been £12.6 billion lower this year with earnings-linked uprating
tl-cost-rf-gross-2026.qualifications: The report attributes the figure to the Office for Budget Responsibility, and we did not find it in the reports we read. The report's summary describes the comparison as a smoothed earnings link.

dwp-2030-poverty-2050.definition: The department's projection of the share of pensioners in relative low income after housing costs in 2049 to 2050, under the rule announced for April 2030.
dwp-2030-poverty-2050.population: People above State Pension age, as modelled by the department.
dwp-2030-poverty-2050.qualifications: A projection from the department's model, Pensim3, under the rule announced for April 2030. Relative low income means household income below 60% of the median of the time. The department says the results depend on its assumptions and are not predictions. The projection is measured against 2024 to 2025, not against keeping the triple lock. The department gives the figure as approximate: around.
dwp-2030-poverty-2050.next_review: When the department publishes the poverty projection against keeping the triple lock, or when the Office for Budget Responsibility costs the change.

tl-cost-ifs-2026.label: Extra yearly spending from the triple lock, 2026 estimate
tl-cost-ifs-2026.definition: The estimated extra State Pension spending in 2026-27 because of the triple lock since 2011, compared with uprating by average earnings.
tl-cost-ifs-2026.passage: the old triple lock has increased annual state pension expenditure by £16 billion by 2026–27 compared with indexation in line with average earnings growth
tl-cost-ifs-2026.qualifications: A difference from a counterfactual. The authors leave out the suspension of 2022 and the use of the Retail Prices Index in 2011.
tl-cost-ifs-2026.next_review: Each April. It comes from a single study, so it changes only if the Institute for Fiscal Studies publishes newer work that replaces it.

rule-2030-counterfactual-ifs-2026.label: How much lower spending would be if the announced rule had applied since 2011
rule-2030-counterfactual-ifs-2026.definition: The estimated amount by which State Pension spending in 2026-27 would be lower if the rule announced for April 2030 had applied in place of the triple lock.
rule-2030-counterfactual-ifs-2026.passage: If the new triple lock had been in place instead, expenditure in 2026–27 would be £9 billion lower than it currently is.
rule-2030-counterfactual-ifs-2026.qualifications: A look back over 15 years, to show scale. It is not a forecast of the saving after 2030.
rule-2030-counterfactual-ifs-2026.next_review: Each April. It comes from a single study, so it changes only if the Institute for Fiscal Studies publishes newer work that replaces it.

rule-2030-real-rise-ifs.label: Real rise in the pension if the announced rule had applied from 2010 to 2026
rule-2030-real-rise-ifs.definition: How much faster than prices the State Pension would have risen between 2010 and 2026 under the rule announced for April 2030.
rule-2030-real-rise-ifs.passage: if the new triple lock had been in place between 2010 and 2026, the state pension would still have risen in real terms (i.e. faster than inflation) by 6%
rule-2030-real-rise-ifs.qualifications: A look back, to show how the rule behaves. It is not a forecast.
rule-2030-real-rise-ifs.next_review: Each April. It comes from a single study, so it changes only if the Institute for Fiscal Studies publishes newer work that replaces it.

rule-2030-vs-tl-rf.label: How much lower the pension would be this year if the announced rule had applied since 2012
rule-2030-vs-tl-rf.definition: The gap between the State Pension this year and what it would be if the rule announced for April 2030 had applied since 2012.
rule-2030-vs-tl-rf.passage: If the new mechanism had been in place since 2012 it would have left the State Pension 4.5 per cent higher than just a link to earnings, but 5.9 per cent lower than it is with the triple lock this year
rule-2030-vs-tl-rf.qualifications: A look back, to show scale. The press release gives no method. It is not a forecast of the gap after 2030.
rule-2030-vs-tl-rf.next_review: Each April. It comes from a single study, so it changes only if the Resolution Foundation publishes newer work that replaces it.

rule-2030-vs-earnings-rf.label: How much higher the pension would be than under an earnings link if the announced rule had applied since 2012
rule-2030-vs-earnings-rf.definition: The gap between the State Pension under the rule announced for April 2030 and under a link to earnings alone, if either had applied since 2012.
rule-2030-vs-earnings-rf.passage: If the new mechanism had been in place since 2012 it would have left the State Pension 4.5 per cent higher than just a link to earnings, but 5.9 per cent lower than it is with the triple lock this year
rule-2030-vs-earnings-rf.qualifications: A look back, to show scale. The press release gives no method.
rule-2030-vs-earnings-rf.next_review: Each April. It comes from a single study, so it changes only if the Resolution Foundation publishes newer work that replaces it.
